FrostByte 1.0 Terms

Effective November 23, 2026 · Version frostbyte-terms-2026-11-23-v1

These terms cover FrostByte provided by Blackfrost Softwares Corp, operating as Blackfrost AI/SI, including its macOS, Windows and Linux desktop apps and optional device companions. Read the bundled software license and third-party notices as well as these terms.

The essentials: peer-to-peer transfers can expose your network address and upload data; third-party files can be unsafe or restricted; and connected companions can keep running after your desktop disconnects. Keep independent backups and use only devices and content you are authorized to access.

1. Agreement and software permissions

Selecting the acceptance checkbox and “Accept and continue” confirms your agreement to these terms and acknowledgment of the privacy notice. If accepting for a business or team, you confirm that you may do so on its behalf. If you do not agree, quit without using FrostByte. Acceptance is recorded locally with the notice versions and time. Earlier local acceptance records are retained when notices change.

Until acceptance, FrostByte does not start its desktop transfer engine. An independently running remote companion may continue working. Declining or closing the welcome screen does not erase downloads or stop another device.

FrostByte Community 1.0 software and its bundled companion are licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. The included LICENSE and NOTICE identify the grant and attribution. These usage and safety notices do not add restrictions to, or revoke, rights granted by Apache-2.0 or third-party licenses. Downloaded files and services have their own permissions. Do not share credentials or private historical Founders builds.

Community source code is announced to become public on Monday 23 November 2026, with updates and pull requests managed regularly by Blackfrost AI/SI. The Community 1.0 license applies now to the software distributed with it. This announcement does not publish the private repository early or relicense private historical Founders releases, artifacts or documentation. Community source will be published under Apache-2.0.

Third-party components keep their own licenses and notices. Nothing in these terms restricts rights granted by those licenses or rights that applicable law does not allow us to restrict. Third-party model weights, datasets, software and other downloaded files remain subject to their owners’ licenses and restrictions.

2. Files, permissions and peer-to-peer sharing

Use FrostByte lawfully and only to download, store or share content you are entitled to use in that way. Follow copyright, model and dataset licenses, access restrictions and network rules. Public access to a file or possession of an access token does not necessarily permit redistribution or commercial use.

BitTorrent peers, trackers and discovery participants can learn network addresses, ports and identifiers for torrents you join. Torrents can upload pieces while downloading and continue seeding afterward. Review sharing, discovery, bandwidth and seeding settings. Your desktop and each companion have separate transfers. Selecting individual files can still transfer portions of neighboring files where torrent pieces overlap.

IPFS is a separate public peer-to-peer network. Previewing or retrieving a CID makes network requests. Downloading uses a receiving node with block serving disabled. Explicit sharing creates a separate publishing copy of selected files. Sharing stops while its allowed content changes and must be enabled again after a FrostByte process restart. Caches use extra storage. Torrent limits and schedules do not govern IPFS traffic.

FrostByte is not an anonymity service. Adding an existing WireGuard overlay as a discovery source does not make all FrostByte traffic use that tunnel. Your operating system’s configured routes determine connectivity.

FrostByte does not certify downloaded material as safe, lawful, accurate, compatible or fit for a purpose. A matching transfer hash or publisher signature does not establish those qualities. Treat models, configurations, archives and scripts as untrusted until assessed. You decide what to open, load or run.

3. Hugging Face and other services

Use only accounts and tokens you are authorized to use. Hugging Face requests remain subject to its terms, account permissions, file licenses and publisher approvals. Revoke tokens through Hugging Face when needed; removing a saved token in FrostByte does not revoke it at the provider.

Catalog hosts, trackers, peers, storage providers, GitHub and linked websites operate independently. Availability, content, security and limits can change. FrostByte cannot guarantee a file or service remains available.

FrostByte is an independent Blackfrost AI/SI product and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NVIDIA, Hugging Face, Apple, Microsoft or the owners of downloaded files. Third-party names identify compatible products and belong to their owners.

4. Connected devices, storage and network discovery

Only connect to or scan devices and networks you own or have permission to administer. Review destinations and permissions before approving discovery, setup or transfers. Discovery does not grant authority to access discovered services.

Companion setup can install or update software, register selected storage folders and add a dedicated public SSH key. Existing SSH connections use your configured credentials and permissions. Verify the device’s SSH identity before trusting it. Adding an existing WireGuard overlay does not copy private keys, start tunnels or change VPN routes.

Companions can read and write registered folders and operate requested downloads and sharing. They run independently and can continue transfers, seeding, storage use and electricity or network costs after the desktop disconnects. Adding storage can restart a companion. Removing the desktop app does not uninstall remote software, remove its authorized SSH key or delete remote downloads.

Check available space and exact destinations before large transfers. Software faults, interruption, drive removal or conflicting writes can leave incomplete data or cause loss. You are responsible for backups, permissions, storage and third-party costs.

Compatible AEON devices may offer browser-based console tools with their own authentication and permissions. Selecting the AEON appearance grants no device access and does not automatically run models.

5. Publisher identities and updates

Publisher identity setup is optional and does not publish files. Protect its password, recovery phrase and backup. A signature identifies a signing key, not safety, legality, accuracy or endorsement. Anyone with the recovery phrase can reproduce the key.

Review the security and platform details accompanying each installer. Signing and notarization can differ by platform and release. Keep operating-system protections enabled; do not bypass warnings for an installer of uncertain origin. Check official release checksums and contact support if unsure.

Update checks retrieve release metadata, not model history. Downloading or installing an update is a separate choice. Private Founders builds are not supplied by the public Community updater.

6. Responsibility and mandatory rights

Software can contain defects, consume unexpected resources, lose or corrupt data or stop working with services or operating-system changes. Do not use FrostByte for safety-critical work or as your only copy of important files. Regular maintenance does not promise a particular response time, feature, compatibility, uptime or uninterrupted service.

Where applicable law permits, software is provided “as is” and “as available,” without express or implied warranties, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose or non-infringement. To the extent permitted by law, Blackfrost AI/SI is not responsible for indirect or consequential losses, lost profits or loss of data arising from use.

Nothing excludes or limits liability, a warranty, guarantee, remedy or consumer right that cannot lawfully be excluded or limited. This includes non-excludable protection relating to fraud, intentional misconduct, personal injury, negligence or statutory remedies. Unenforceable provisions do not override mandatory law.

FrostByte 1.0 has no analytics, automatic diagnostic-report or in-app feedback collection. Feedback is optional and takes place on GitHub if you choose to submit it. Not providing feedback does not limit the app.

We may publish revised notices with updated versions and dates. Material app-notice changes are presented for review when acceptance is required. Download websites and third-party services have their own applicable notices.

7. Contact

For licensing, security, access or privacy questions, contact support@blackfrostai.com. Do not include passwords, private SSH keys, access tokens, recovery phrases or sensitive files in public issues or support messages.
privacy:
FrostByte 1.0 Privacy Notice

Effective October 12, 2026 · Version frostbyte-privacy-2026-10-12-v1 · macOS, Windows and Linux

FrostByte is provided by Blackfrost Softwares Corp, operating as Blackfrost AI/SI.

No analytics, automatic diagnostic reports or in-app feedback collection. FrostByte 1.0 has no reporting transport: it does not collect diagnostic counters for submission, send reports to the former backend or upload feedback. An earlier diagnostics opt-in cannot enable this retired functionality. Optional feedback opens GitHub without automatically attaching application data.

This is not a claim of anonymous or network-free operation. Local application state and device dashboards are needed to run the app. Transfers, approved connections, update checks and services you use still exchange ordinary network data.

1. What stays on your devices

FrostByte stores settings, destinations, catalog and library entries, hidden-entry choices, torrent metadata and identifiers, transfer progress, Hugging Face repository and file information, and saved device connection details so your session can resume. It stores your accepted notice versions and acceptance time locally. Previous acceptance records remain when notices change; their historical diagnostics choice cannot enable reporting.

Interface preferences live in the local application profile. Device dashboards read resource, storage and transfer measurements from this computer or an approved companion. These are displayed locally and are not submitted to Blackfrost AI/SI as analytics.

On macOS, Community records normally live under ~/Library/Application Support/frostbyte, with Electron interface data under ~/Library/Application Support/Frost/Byte. Windows uses %APPDATA%\\frostbyte and the edition’s Electron profile. Linux uses the configured application-data and interface profile directories. Founders uses a separate edition profile. Download destinations can be changed. Local filenames, paths, hostnames and transfer history are not all encrypted.

Operational logs may contain filenames, repository names, device information or paths. FrostByte 1.0 does not automatically submit logs, crash dumps, screenshots or recordings. Operating systems, dependencies and connected services may create their own records. Review anything you manually share with support.

2. Credentials and publisher identity

New saved Hugging Face tokens and pairing private SSH keys use Electron safeStorage with operating-system protection: Keychain-backed encryption on macOS, the Windows user’s DPAPI context on Windows, and an available supported credential store on Linux. FrostByte refuses new secret storage when secure encryption is unavailable or a plaintext backend is selected. This cannot protect secrets from a compromised account, system or software that already has authorized access.

FrostByte can retain Hugging Face account and token-role metadata. Older records may need migration; removing a token in Settings clears the app’s stored token fields. Revocation at Hugging Face is separate.

A companion-setup password is used in memory and is not saved as the reconnect credential. Approved pairing adds a public SSH key to the device and retains the matching protected private key locally. Saved details include addresses, username, port and trusted host identity. Existing SSH aliases use your existing configuration and credentials.

Publisher identity setup optionally stores a public key, display name, creation time, backup confirmation and protected private key locally. Its password and recovery phrase are not uploaded by setup. A recovery phrase restores the same key; protect it like a secret. Copying it can expose it to your clipboard or clipboard-history software. Removing the identity does not erase copies saved elsewhere.

Account changes, credential-store locking or app updates can affect stored-secret access. FrostByte preserves unavailable encrypted records for recovery instead of silently replacing them.

3. Transfer and discovery requests

Hugging Face: searches, filters, repository identifiers, revisions, filenames and downloads go to Hugging Face and its delivery infrastructure. Approved authenticated operations include your token. Providers receive the requesting device’s network address and ordinary request metadata.

BitTorrent: peers, trackers, DHT and enabled local discovery can receive IP addresses, ports, peer identifiers, torrent infohashes, transfer information and shared pieces. Downloads can upload and continue seeding.

IPFS: previewing or retrieving a CID exposes requested content identifiers and connection information to relevant participants. Explicitly shared content is served from a separate publishing cache. Files, verification records, history and caches remain on the transferring device until cleared. Clearing history or cache does not automatically delete completed downloads.

Catalogs and publication: importing a catalog contacts its host. Exporting magnets or CSVs creates content identifiers or metadata for you to save or share. Publication is a separate explicit action; review what will be sent and where. Public data you share can be copied and cannot necessarily be recalled.

Local and overlay discovery: approved network checks communicate with selected addresses and can read service greetings. Adding an existing WireGuard overlay records its discovery selection locally; it does not read or copy WireGuard private keys or change routes. Operating-system routing determines actual connectivity. Enabled port mapping communicates with your router.

Requests originate from the device doing the work: the desktop for local transfers or the companion for remote transfers. FrostByte does not hide that address or guarantee anonymity.

4. Connected devices and optional model services

Approved SSH or paired connections exchange device capabilities, folder paths, storage status, transfer commands and results. A companion can read and write registered storage folders and retains transfer and inventory state there. Authenticated Hugging Face downloads can send the approved token to that companion for the job; current companion download records do not persist it.

Companions can continue after the desktop disconnects or is removed. Device administrators and sufficiently privileged software can access that device’s state and files. Removing a desktop profile does not uninstall remote software or remove its authorized SSH key.

AEON capabilities and console links arrive over an approved connection. Opening a console contacts the device in your browser and uses its own login. Changing the appearance does not grant access or send analytics.

Where your edition provides Studio or model-service connections, prompts, selected context, messages and approved tool results go to the local or remote model endpoint you choose. Conversations and project state may be saved locally. Provider authentication and data policies apply to that endpoint. These functional exchanges are not FrostByte analytics.

5. Update checks, links and optional GitHub feedback

Enabled automatic update checking and manual checks request public release metadata from Blackfrost AI/SI’s update service. Requests do not attach library history, model identifiers, credentials or an installation identifier. Hosting infrastructure receives ordinary metadata such as the network address and time. You can disable automatic checks in Settings. Founders does not use the public Community updater.

Selecting feedback opens the official GitHub issue page in your browser with no prefilled report, diagnostics, logs, filenames, token or account data from FrostByte. GitHub receives the browser request under its own privacy policy. You decide whether to sign in, write and submit an issue. Public repository issues can be visible to everyone; do not include secrets or sensitive data. FrostByte cannot erase copies others make.

Other links open their destination in your browser under its operator’s policies. Contacting support sends the address and content you choose to provide. Declining feedback does not reduce functionality.

6. Website delivery and earlier releases

This notice describes the v1.0 app. Download websites, GitHub, cloud storage and service infrastructure can process IP addresses, user agents, URLs, timestamps, response information, session cookies and security records under their displayed policies. No app analytics or report collection does not mean those services receive no network requests.

Installing v1.0 stops the retired reporting path; it does not delete reports already submitted by older versions, support correspondence or independent service logs. Contact support about records previously submitted to Blackfrost AI/SI. This update does not silently change website retention settings or erase server-side records.

7. Retention and choices

Local records remain until cleared or removed. Removing transfers, hiding entries, uninstalling the desktop or clearing IPFS caches does not necessarily delete completed files, settings, backups or companion state. File deletion has a separate explicit review.

You may remove a saved Hugging Face token, revoke it with its provider, retire an authorized SSH key, disconnect a companion, disable automatic update checks or pause/stop sharing. Verify the affected device and file scope. Previous sharing cannot be recalled from independent peers.

Where applicable, you may have rights to information, access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection or other remedies regarding personal data we control. Contact support to make a request. Proportionate verification may be needed. We cannot directly erase records on your devices or independently operated peers and services.

8. Contact and changes

Contact Blackfrost Softwares Corp, operating as Blackfrost AI/SI, at support@blackfrostai.com without sending secrets. Material changes to app data handling will be reflected in versioned notices and presented for review.
